Metric and observed evidence: MSC energy. Wireless-device study reports 10.28 mWh cm⁻³ at 766.5 mW cm⁻³ [2].
Explicit bound or target: Ideal constant-capacitance energy is ½C(Vₘₐₓ² − Vₘᵢₙ²) within a specified usable window.
Basis, limitation and next measurement: Use matched two-electrode C at the working rate and volume basis. Quantify terminal energy using the loaded discharge.

Metric and observed evidence: Hybrid energy. Same cell reports 145.4 and 79.72 μWh cm⁻² at 0.75 and 7.5 mA cm⁻² [141].
Explicit bound or target: Charge balance and individual electrode potential windows determine the reversible limit.
Basis, limitation and next measurement: The higher-rate result retains about 54.8% of lower-rate energy. This within-study rate comparison is not a thermodynamic gap.

Metric and observed evidence: Zn battery capacity. Printed comparator reports about 1.3 mAh cm⁻² at 0.1 mA cm⁻² [22].
Explicit bound or target: Zn → Zn²⁺ + 2e⁻ corresponds to about 820 mAh g⁻¹ of Zn for that reaction.
Basis, limitation and next measurement: Area-normalized full-cell capacity and isolated Zn stoichiometric capacity are incompatible bases. Determine accessible inventory and limiting balanced charge.

Metric and observed evidence: Pulse power. Cell, regulator and interconnect share voltage losses.
Explicit bound or target: For a fixed Thevenin model, V²/(4R) is the matched-resistive-load peak. Application requires its stated cutoff.
Basis, limitation and next measurement: Measure local terminal voltage and current throughout the pulse. Report useful power at the duration and converter cutoff.

Metric and observed evidence: Fatigue. Wireless MSC study reports 98.5% capacitance retention after 1,000 biaxial stretch cycles from 0% to 500% areal strain [2].
Explicit bound or target: Service target is retained output over the application's declared mechanical and environmental sequence.
Basis, limitation and next measurement: Areal strain and local electrode strain differ. Record energy and transient sag during cycling under load.

Metric and observed evidence: Damage recovery. Rocking-chair microbattery and healable epidermal gel demonstrate distinct endpoints [12], [177].
Explicit bound or target: Service threshold must specify damage, repair, electrical isolation and recovered usable energy.
Basis, limitation and next measurement: Mechanical, conductive and electrochemical recovery are separate. Pair damage imaging and continuity with a matched terminal discharge.

Metric and observed evidence: End-of-life degradation. Sensor-gel degradation has a materials-level endpoint [177].
Explicit bound or target: Disposal target must specify environment, time and constituent fate.
Basis, limitation and next measurement: Measure mass balance, released species and residual conducting phases. Use-phase integrity requires a separate protocol.
